title: Surah Al-Fatiha
preview: The Opening – the first surah of the Quran, recited in every rakah of prayer. A conversation between you and your Lord.
content:
# Surah Al-Fatiha

*The Opening – 7 verses | Surah 1 – Makki*

**1.** In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

**2.** All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

**3.** The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

**4.** Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.

**5.** It is You we worship and You we ask for help.

**6.** Guide us to the straight path.

**7.** The path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor, not of those who have earned anger or of those who are astray.

---

**Summary (Tarjuma):** Al-Fatiha opens with praise of Allah – the Lord of all worlds, the Merciful, the Master of the Day of Judgment. Then it turns into a direct prayer: we worship Him alone, we ask Him alone for help, and we ask for the straight path – the path of those He has blessed, not of those who earn His anger or go astray. Every time you recite it in salah, you are renewing your reliance on Allah and your request for guidance. It is the essence of the believer’s relationship with Allah.

*Reference: Quran 1:1–7*

title: Surah Al-Ikhlas
preview: The Sincerity – four verses that declare the oneness and uniqueness of Allah. Equal to one-third of the Quran in reward.
content:
# Surah Al-Ikhlas

*The Sincerity – 4 verses | Surah 112 – Makki*

**1.** Say: He is Allah, the One.

**2.** Allah, the Eternal, the Absolute.

**3.** He begets not nor was He begotten.

**4.** And there is none comparable to Him.

---

**Summary (Tarjuma):** Al-Ikhlas is a clear statement of tawheed: Allah is One, unique and absolute. He has no children and was not born; He has no equal or rival. This surah answers who Allah is – no partners, no family, no likeness. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that reciting it is equal in reward to one-third of the Quran. It is often recited after every prayer and before sleep to affirm pure faith in the One God.

*Reference: Quran 112:1–4*

title: Surah Al-Falaq
preview: The Daybreak – seeking refuge in Allah from external evils: creation, darkness, magic, and envy.
content:
# Surah Al-Falaq

*The Daybreak – 5 verses | Surah 113 – Makki*

**1.** Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak

**2.** From the evil of what He has created,

**3.** And from the evil of darkness when it settles,

**4.** And from the evil of those who blow on the knots,

**5.** And from the evil of an envier when he envies.

---

**Summary (Tarjuma):** Al-Falaq is a supplication for protection. We seek refuge in the Lord of the dawn from harm that can come from creation (creatures, calamities), from the darkness of the night, from those who practice magic (blowing on knots), and from the evil of the envier when he envies. It is one of the Mu’awwidhatayn (two surahs of refuge) and is recited with An-Nas and Al-Ikhlas after the fard prayers and before sleep for protection and barakah.

*Reference: Quran 113:1–5*

title: Surah An-Nas
preview: Mankind – seeking refuge in Allah from the whisperer who tempts the heart, from jinn and people.
content:
# Surah An-Nas

*Mankind – 6 verses | Surah 114 – Makki*

**1.** Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,

**2.** The Sovereign of mankind,

**3.** The God of mankind,

**4.** From the evil of the retreating whisperer,

**5.** Who whispers into the breasts of mankind,

**6.** From among the jinn and mankind.

---

**Summary (Tarjuma):** An-Nas asks Allah for protection from the “whisperer” – the one who casts evil suggestions into the hearts of people. He may be from the jinn or from mankind. We seek refuge in the Lord, King, and God of mankind, who alone can guard the heart from these whispers. Together with Al-Falaq and Al-Ikhlas, this surah is recited for spiritual protection and to ward off evil and envy.

*Reference: Quran 114:1–6*

title: Ayatul Kursi
preview: The greatest verse in the Quran – the Verse of the Throne. It describes Allah’s majesty and is recited for protection and blessing.
content:
# Ayatul Kursi (Verse of the Throne)

*Quran 2:255*

Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass not of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.

---

**Summary (Tarjuma):** Ayatul Kursi declares that Allah is the only God – alive forever, sustaining everything. He does not sleep or tire. Everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. No one can intercede except with His leave, and His knowledge is beyond what any creation can grasp. His Throne (Kursi) encompasses the heavens and the earth. Reciting it after every prayer and before sleep brings protection, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said it is the greatest verse in the Quran.

*Reference: Quran 2:255*
